statements.status_notes: CVE-2010-0928 is the 2010 RSA-CRT fault-injection attack (Pellegrini et al.): recovering a private key requires physically inducing computational faults (voltage/clock manipulation) in the CPU while it performs RSA operations. There is no remote or local-software attack vector; OpenSSL upstream disputes the issue (fault injection is outside its threat model per the OpenSSL security policy) and Debian has marked it unimportant with no fix planned since 2010. A container boundary offers no surface for hardware fault injection beyond what the host already implies. In datahub-ingestion the non-fips variants install the Debian openssl package (3.5.6-1~deb13u2, pulled in via ca-certificates) and the fips variants ship the dhi pkg-openssl 3.5.7 rebuild; the analysis is identical for both.

There is no remote or local-software attack vector; OpenSSL upstream disputes the issue (fault injection is outside its threat model per the OpenSSL security policy) and Debian has marked it unimportant with no fix planned since 2010. A container boundary offers no surface for hardware fault injection beyond what the host already implies. In datahub-ingestion the non-fips variants install the Debian openssl package (3.5.6-1~deb13u2, pulled in via ca-certificates) and the fips variants ship the dhi pkg-openssl 3.5.7 rebuild; the analysis is identical for both.
Marked no-dsa by Debian Security Team; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-42767

Fault injection based attacks are not within OpenSSLs threat model according to the security policy and this CVE is not treated as security bug by upstream: https://www.openssl.org/policies/general/security-policy.html

This CVE is only affecting installation on PowerPC architecture and even then is this CVE disputed because the OpenSSL security policy explicitly notes that any side channels which require same physical system to be detected are outside of the threat model for the software. The timing signal is so small that it is infeasible to be detected without having the attacking process running on the same physical system.
